From Har Ki Pauri to Ganga Aarti Ceremony and Mansa Devi Temple, the best places to visit in Haridwar blend iconic landmarks with quiet corners most travelers miss. This travel guide to Haridwar brings together 25 top tourist attractions in Haridwar, hand-ranked by popularity and real visitor reviews, so you can plan with confidence. We have also tucked in genuine hidden gems like Shanti Ghat (Shanti Van) after the headline sights, because the most memorable moments in Haridwar often happen off the obvious trail. pageContent: Haridwar ranks among Uttarakhand's most rewarding destinations, and it is easy to see why travelers keep returning. Known for where the ganga touches the plains and salvation begins, it packs a remarkable variety of experiences into one trip. When people search for the best places to visit in Haridwar, the headline names come up again and again: Har Ki Pauri, Ganga Aarti Ceremony, Mansa Devi Temple, Chandi Devi Temple, Rajaji National Park. Each earns its spot for a reason — together they capture the pilgrimage, spiritual, heritage character that defines the region.

Beyond the icons, the must visit places in Haridwar reward anyone willing to explore a little further. Spots such as Daksha Mahadev Temple, Haridwar Main Bazaar (Bara Bazaar), Shantikunj (Gayatri Pariwar Ashram), Parmarth Niketan (Rishikesh, nearby), Maya Devi Temple round out an itinerary and show a different side of the destination. For the best experience, time your visit thoughtfully: many of the top tourist attractions in Haridwar are at their finest early in the day or around golden hour, when the light is soft, crowds are thin, and photographs come alive. Most travelers find that two to four unhurried days are enough to cover the essentials without rushing.

Looking for things to do in Haridwar that go beyond the guidebook? Seek out the quieter finds — Gau Ghat and Paon Dhara, Crystal World (Haridwar Mineral Market), Shanti Ghat (Shanti Van) — where you will trade ticket queues for genuine local atmosphere. This curated guide is built to be the most useful starting point on the internet for your trip: every attraction below includes why it is worth your time, the best time to visit, a realistic duration, and a direct Google Maps search. Use it to shortlist your favourites, then drop them straight into a Trypinn itinerary, invite your crew, and turn a list of must-see places in Haridwar into a trip that actually happens.

Planning practicalities matter as much as the sights. A typical visit to Haridwar in Uttarakhand works best as a two-to-four-day trip, leaving room to slow down rather than tick boxes. Group the Har Ki Pauri and Ganga Aarti Ceremony area together to cut travel time, and keep a relaxed half-day spare for the hidden gems and spontaneous detours that make pilgrimage and spiritual and heritage so memorable. Whatever season you choose, book stays and any permits or tickets ahead during peak months, start early to beat the crowds, and carry the Google Maps links below so navigating between the best places to visit in Haridwar stays effortless from the first attraction to the last.

attractions.name: Har Ki Pauri
attractions.description: Har Ki Pauri — 'Steps of Vishnu' — is Haridwar's holiest ghat, built at the precise point where the Ganga is believed to exit the mountains and enter the plains of India. The main ghat is anchored by a footprint of Vishnu embedded in a stone wall, perpetually submerged in the sacred river. Every evening at sunset, dozens of priests simultaneously swing flaming torches and conch shells in the Ganga Aarti ceremony, sending thousands of flower-and-flame diyas drifting downstream. The Kumbh Mela's largest gatherings take place here.
attractions.whyVisit: The holiest single point on the Ganga and the venue for India's most celebrated daily religious ceremony — an experience that overwhelms the senses.
attractions.bestTime: Sunset for the Ganga Aarti; October to March for comfortable crowds.

attractions.name: Ganga Aarti Ceremony
attractions.description: The evening Ganga Aarti at Har Ki Pauri is performed simultaneously by dozens of priests at the top of the clock at sunset, every single day without exception. Rows of priests in saffron robes raise massive multi-tiered oil lamps in synchronised arcs over the river while bells ring, conches blow, and thousands of pilgrims crowd the ghats. The ceremony lasts 45 minutes, ending as fleets of leaf-and-marigold diyas float downstream. The evening sky, the firelight, and the river create an atmosphere of extraordinary spiritual intensity.
attractions.whyVisit: One of the most emotionally powerful religious ceremonies on earth — a daily ritual that has run for centuries without pause.
attractions.bestTime: Daily at sunset; timings vary by season (roughly 6-7 PM).

attractions.name: Mansa Devi Temple
attractions.description: Perched atop Bilwa Parvat at 1,073 feet, Mansa Devi temple is one of the Panch Tirthas (five sacred sites) of Haridwar, dedicated to the goddess Mansa, a form of Shakti believed to fulfil wishes. The steep hill is reached by a ropeway (udan khatola) or a 1.5 km climb of 476 steps through dense scrub forest. Devotees tie a sacred thread to the trees lining the approach and return to untie it once their wish is granted. The temple terrace offers the best panoramic view of Haridwar, the Ganga, and the Siwalik hills.
attractions.whyVisit: The best elevated view over Haridwar and the first glimpse of the Ganga as it sweeps through the plains — reached by scenic cable car.
attractions.bestTime: October to March; early morning to avoid ropeway queues.

attractions.name: Chandi Devi Temple
attractions.description: Chandi Devi temple crowns the Neel Parvat hill on the east bank of the Ganga, accessible by an 8th-century stone staircase of 3 km or by ropeway from Chandi Ghat. The presiding deity Chandi Devi is one of the Siddha Peethas of India — sacred sites where Shakti's body fell according to Hindu cosmology. The temple was built by the Raja of Kashmir in 1929. From the hilltop, the entire Haridwar valley, the bend of the Ganga, and the Rajaji National Park forest spread out below.
attractions.whyVisit: A Siddha Peetha temple with a commanding hilltop position — the twin sacred peak to Mansa Devi on the opposite bank of the Ganga.
attractions.bestTime: October to March; Navratri (April and October) for festivals.

attractions.name: Rajaji National Park
attractions.description: Rajaji National Park begins virtually at Haridwar's northern boundary and covers 820 square kilometres of sal forest, riverine grassland, and lower Siwalik hills. It is home to over 500 elephants — one of the largest herds in North India — as well as tigers, leopards, sloth bears, king cobras, and gharial in the Ganga tributaries. Jeep safaris from the Chilla range are easily combined with a Haridwar pilgrimage. The park is also superb for birding, with over 300 species including great hornbills and fish eagles.
attractions.whyVisit: A world-class wildlife sanctuary beginning at Haridwar's city limits — India's only place to combine Ganga pilgrimage and wild elephant safaris on the same day.
attractions.bestTime: November to June; park closed July to October during monsoon.

attractions.name: Daksha Mahadev Temple
attractions.description: Located in Kankhal, 4 km south of Haridwar, Daksha Mahadev temple occupies the site where, according to Hindu mythology, King Daksha performed the yagna (fire sacrifice) that caused Sati, Shiva's consort, to immolate herself — triggering the cosmic grief that led to the entire Sati Peetha tradition. The present temple was built in the early 20th century on ancient foundations and houses images of Shiva, Sati, and a large Daksha figure. Kankhal is also a significant centre of ashrams and Sanskrit scholarship.
attractions.whyVisit: The mythological ground zero of the Shakti Peetha tradition — a living sacred site directly linked to one of Hinduism's foundational cosmic narratives.
attractions.bestTime: Year-round; Mahashivratri for peak pilgrimage activity.

attractions.name: Haridwar Main Bazaar (Bara Bazaar)
attractions.description: Haridwar's main commercial artery stretches for 2 km parallel to the Ganga from Moti Bazaar to Jwalapur, packed with shops selling brass and copper puja vessels, sacred Ganga Jal in clay pots, rudraksha malas, sandalwood, religious prints, and local specialities like thandai, chaas, and Haridwar's distinctive aloo ki sabzi. The bazaar is most vivid early morning and at dusk, when pilgrims fresh from the ghats throng the narrow lanes. The smell of incense, camphor, and marigolds permeates the entire market.
attractions.whyVisit: The most vibrant and aromatic pilgrimage bazaar in North India — a sensory journey through 2,000 years of sacred commerce on the Ganga.
attractions.bestTime: Early morning and evening; October to March for comfortable temperatures.

attractions.name: Shantikunj (Gayatri Pariwar Ashram)
attractions.description: Shantikunj, the headquarters of the All World Gayatri Pariwar established by Pandit Shriram Sharma Acharya, is one of India's largest reform Hindu ashrams and a UNESCO-noted cultural institution. Set on the Ganga's bank north of Haridwar, its campus houses a Gayatri temple, yagna shala, extensive gardens, and guest accommodation for thousands. The ashram runs Sanskrit courses, Vedic yagna training, and wellness programmes open to non-Hindi speakers. The morning group Gayatri havan is a remarkable introduction to Vedic practice.
attractions.whyVisit: The world's largest centre for Vedic yagna practice — an authentic and inclusive ashram environment for serious spiritual seekers.
attractions.bestTime: Year-round; stay of 2-3 nights recommended for full experience.

attractions.name: Parmarth Niketan (Rishikesh, nearby)
attractions.description: Parmarth Niketan on the Rishikesh ghat is the largest ashram in Rishikesh, 25 km from Haridwar, housing over 1,000 monks and presiding over the most famous Ganga Aarti in the Rishikesh-Haridwar corridor. The ashram complex is famous for its 10-metre statue of Shiva standing in the Ganga, the garden of spiritual figures along the riverbank, and the International Yoga Festival held each March. The evening aarti at the ashram's ghat is smaller and more intimate than Haridwar's Har Ki Pauri.
attractions.whyVisit: The spiritual centrepiece of Rishikesh — the best evening ghat ceremony in the 25 km Haridwar-Rishikesh sacred corridor.
attractions.bestTime: Year-round; March for the International Yoga Festival.

attractions.name: Maya Devi Temple
attractions.description: Maya Devi is one of the oldest temples in Haridwar, believed to date from the 11th century, and is listed as one of the Shakti Peethas — sites where parts of Sati's body fell from the sky. The deity here is Maya Devi (an eight-armed form of Durga), and the temple is considered the Adhisthhatri Devi (presiding goddess) of Haridwar itself. The stone image in the sanctum is believed to be Swaroop Murti (self-manifested) rather than human-carved, giving it supreme sanctity. The temple is at the heart of the ancient city.
attractions.whyVisit: The oldest and most sacred resident goddess temple of Haridwar — a Shakti Peetha that predates every other major structure in the city.
attractions.bestTime: Year-round; Navratri for peak pilgrimage.

attractions.name: Bhimgoda Tank
attractions.description: Bhimgoda Tank is a sacred tank adjacent to the Ganga near Har Ki Pauri, associated with the Mahabharata hero Bhima who is said to have created it by striking his knee (bhim goda means 'Bhima's knee') on the ground to create a water source. The tank is fed by the Ganga and contains turtles, sacred fish, and lotus plants. Pilgrims complete a ritual circuit of the tank after bathing at Har Ki Pauri. The surrounding ghats and old temples are among the most architecturally layered in Haridwar.
attractions.whyVisit: A Mahabharata-era sacred tank at the heart of Haridwar's most ancient ghat complex — steeped in epic mythology and living ritual.
attractions.bestTime: Year-round; early morning for the most serene atmosphere.

attractions.name: Patanjali Yogpeeth
attractions.description: Patanjali Yogpeeth, established by yoga guru Baba Ramdev and Acharya Balkrishna, is one of the world's largest yoga research institutions, occupying a vast campus 5 km from Haridwar. The main campus includes a massive yoga and meditation hall seating 60,000 practitioners, Ayurvedic research laboratories, herbal gardens, and the Patanjali Naturopathy Hospital. Daily early-morning yoga sessions are open to the public and free of charge. The campus layout and scale give a sense of the extraordinary scale of the contemporary yoga movement.
attractions.whyVisit: The world's largest purpose-built yoga institution and the headquarters of India's most widely practised modern yoga movement.
attractions.bestTime: Year-round; morning sessions at 5:30 AM for the yoga class.

attractions.name: Sapt Rishi Ashram and Ghat
attractions.description: Sapt Rishi Ghat, 5 km upstream from Haridwar, marks the point where the Ganga is believed to have divided into seven streams to avoid disturbing the meditation of the seven great rishis (sages) of Hindu tradition. The ashram complex on the bank includes a meditation cave associated with Swami Vivekananda, an old Shiva temple, and a calm ghat far removed from the crowds of Har Ki Pauri. The Ganga here is broad and fast-moving, and the surrounding forest creates a contemplative atmosphere.
attractions.whyVisit: The most peaceful ghat in the Haridwar area — a mythological landmark where the Ganga respectfully changed course for seven sages.
attractions.bestTime: Early morning year-round.

attractions.name: Swami Vivekananda Park
attractions.description: Swami Vivekananda Park on the Ganga bank in Haridwar is a large, well-maintained public garden with a commanding statue of Swami Vivekananda on a riverfront terrace. The park provides one of the best pedestrian vantage points over the Ganga's broad channel as it swings around the Haridwar bend. In the early morning, families, sadhus, and early-rising pilgrims gather here to watch the mist rise from the river before the day's heat begins. The park also marks the start of the riverside promenade walk.
attractions.whyVisit: The best morning riverfront promenade in Haridwar, with wide Ganga views and a significant Vivekananda memorial.
attractions.bestTime: Dawn year-round.

attractions.name: Kumbh Mela Grounds
attractions.description: Haridwar hosts the Kumbh Mela — the world's largest human gathering — every 12 years (with Ardha Kumbh every 6 years and Kanwar Mela annually). The permanent infrastructure of the Kumbh grounds extends several kilometres along both banks of the Ganga. Even between Kumbh years, the vast pontoon bridge footings, the akharas (monastic orders' camps), and the extensive ghat networks are all visible and accessible. The scale of organisation required to host 20-50 million pilgrims over 6 weeks is itself a remarkable thing to witness.
attractions.whyVisit: The venue of the world's largest gathering of humanity — the physical infrastructure of the Kumbh is awe-inspiring even in off years.
attractions.bestTime: Kumbh and Ardha Kumbh years; Kanwar Mela in July-August for the annual mega-pilgrimage.

attractions.name: Rishikesh (Laxman Jhula and Ram Jhula)
attractions.description: Laxman Jhula is a 450-foot iron suspension bridge over the Ganga at Rishikesh, 25 km from Haridwar, originally built in 1929 on the site where Lakshmana crossed the river on a jute bridge in the Ramayana. Ram Jhula, 2 km south, is a wider 1986-era bridge lined with shrines. Both bridges are surrounded by multi-storey ashrams built into the cliff face, temple chanting pouring from every window. Crossing either bridge at dawn, with the ice-cold Himalayan Ganga roaring below, is genuinely breathtaking.
attractions.whyVisit: The two most iconic images of Rishikesh — suspension bridges over the sacred Ganga framed by Himalayan ashrams on both banks.
attractions.bestTime: Year-round; dawn and dusk for the best light and atmosphere.

attractions.name: Ganga Canal Head Works
attractions.description: The Haridwar Barrage and the original 19th-century Ganga Canal Head Works, built by Colonel Proby Cautley of the East India Company between 1842 and 1854, represents one of the greatest engineering achievements of the Victorian era. The Upper Ganga Canal, which extends 560 km from this point to Kanpur, irrigates 3 million acres of the Gangetic plains. The original brick-and-lime stonework of the head works is still intact and functioning. A small museum at the site explains the canal's construction and hydrological impact.
attractions.whyVisit: A Victorian engineering marvel of global significance — the headworks of the longest irrigation canal in British Indian history.
attractions.bestTime: Year-round; museum open weekdays.

attractions.name: Kushavart Ghat
attractions.description: Kushavart Ghat in Haridwar is associated with the sage Dattatreya and with the ancient custom of preserving ancestral ashes in the Ganga. The ghat is the primary location in Haridwar for the Asthi Visarjan ceremony, in which ashes of cremated relatives are immersed in the sacred river. Brahmin priests called Pandas maintain genealogical records here stretching back in some families for 500 years, recording every Hindu family who has ever performed last rites at this ghat. The records themselves are extraordinary historical documents.
attractions.whyVisit: The ancestral-records ghat where Brahmin pandas hold 500 years of Hindu family genealogies — the most remarkable archival tradition on the Ganga.
attractions.bestTime: Year-round.

attractions.name: Sureshwari Devi Temple (Neel Dhara)
attractions.description: The Sureshwari Devi temple on the Neel Dhara (Blue Stream) tributary between Haridwar and Rishikesh is a relatively little-known goddess temple set at the edge of the Rajaji forest, where the crystal-clear Neel Dhara joins the Ganga. The surrounding jungle brings Rajaji elephants to the river here on some evenings, making this the only place where you can plausibly observe wild elephants with the Ganga in the background. The temple itself is modest but the location is exceptional.
attractions.whyVisit: The only temple in India where wild elephants regularly appear in the sacred river adjacent to the shrine — a remarkable wildlife-spiritual convergence.
attractions.bestTime: November to May (dry season); late afternoon for elephant sightings.

attractions.name: Anjali Aarti Ghat (Birla Ghat)
attractions.description: Birla Ghat, also called Anjali Ghat or Subhash Ghat, is a quieter alternative to the crowds of Har Ki Pauri and runs a smaller but no less sincere evening Ganga Aarti ceremony. The ghat was developed by the Birla family of industrialists as a devotional gift to Haridwar and features wide marble steps, a tall Shiva statue, and a series of brass lamps that are lit at the same moment as the Har Ki Pauri ceremony. Pilgrims who find the main ghat too crowded find Birla Ghat both accessible and genuinely moving.
attractions.whyVisit: The most accessible and uncrowded Ganga Aarti in Haridwar — identical ritual intensity to Har Ki Pauri without the jostling crowds.
attractions.bestTime: Evening at sunset year-round.

attractions.name: Patanjali Chikitsalaya Herbal Garden
attractions.description: The medicinal plant research gardens attached to Patanjali Yogpeeth cultivate over 200 species of Ayurvedic and classical Vedic herbs in labelled beds organised by body system and classical text reference. The garden is open to visitors as part of the Patanjali campus tour and provides an extraordinary introduction to the pharmacopoeia of classical Indian medicine. Plants include rare Himalayan species such as brahmi, ashwagandha, shatavari, and kutki. Guided walks are available in both Hindi and English.
attractions.whyVisit: The world's largest working Ayurvedic herb garden — an educational and sensory tour through 5,000 years of Indian medical botany.
attractions.bestTime: Year-round; morning for guided walks.

attractions.name: Jwalapur Mata Temple
attractions.description: Jwalapur is the southern suburb of Haridwar and home to an ancient Mata temple sacred to the local Jat and Rajput communities of the upper Gangetic plains. The temple is known for its Navratri celebrations which draw pilgrims from across western Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand in numbers that rival Haridwar's main ghats. The neighbourhood itself retains a distinctly Garhwali character, with traditional havelis, an old stepwell, and a morning vegetable market of considerable antiquity.
attractions.whyVisit: A deeply local pilgrimage temple with Navratri celebrations on a scale that most outsiders never encounter in the Haridwar area.
attractions.bestTime: Navratri (April and October) for festivals.

attractions.name: Gau Ghat and Paon Dhara
attractions.description: Gau Ghat is one of Haridwar's oldest river bathing platforms, upstream from Har Ki Pauri, believed to be where the cow goddess Surabhi bathed in the Ganga. The adjacent Paon Dhara is a natural rock platform at river level where the Ganga's current creates an unusually powerful swirling pattern, believed to wash away sins with particular efficacy. Few tourists reach this ghat, making it a place of genuine spiritual quiet. Early-morning bathers here include elderly Haridwar residents who have performed the same ritual daily for decades.
attractions.whyVisit: The most spiritually quiet ghat in Haridwar — a place of authentic daily ritual practice away from tourist infrastructure.
attractions.bestTime: Dawn year-round.

attractions.name: Crystal World (Haridwar Mineral Market)
attractions.description: A cluster of gem and crystal dealers near the Haridwar bus stand sell the finest range of Himalayan mineral specimens in North India — rough amethyst from Rajasthan, rudraksha seeds from Nepal, rose quartz from Himachal, and semi-precious stones sourced from the entire mineral belt of the Himalayas and the Deccan. Serious crystal collectors make Haridwar a regular destination because wholesale prices here are 30-50% below those in Delhi's jewellery markets. The dealers have deep knowledge of the mineral origins and properties.
attractions.whyVisit: The best-value Himalayan crystal and gemstone market in North India — a hidden gem for collectors and a unique Haridwar shopping experience.
attractions.bestTime: Year-round.

attractions.name: Shanti Ghat (Shanti Van)
attractions.description: Shanti Ghat on the upstream edge of Haridwar's ghat network is a recently developed but serene riverside parkway where young deodar trees have been planted along the Ganga bank, creating a shaded walking promenade. The ghat is the venue for the NGO-run Ganga water-quality monitoring programme and several conservation organisations have their Haridwar offices here. The cleanest stretch of the Ganga visible in the city flows past this ghat, and the pebble beach below the steps is accessible at low water for close contact with the river.
attractions.whyVisit: The cleanest and greenest stretch of the Haridwar ghat — a peaceful river walk where serious conservation work and daily spiritual practice coexist.
attractions.bestTime: Early morning year-round.
